title: The NATO phonetic alphabet
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: When a letter is said over a phone or a radio, B, D, P and V can sound the same. The phonetic alphabet gives each letter a word that can't be mistaken. It is handy for spelling a name or a booking code, and it is used every day by pilots, sailors and emergency services.

How to hold it: Twenty-six words is about five chunks of five. Most words start with their own letter, so the letter is the cue and the word is the picture: picture each one as you say it (a bravo crowd cheering, a foxtrot dancer, a golf ball, a hotel, a kilo of flour, a lime from Lima). Link the words of a chunk into a short story: Alfa and Bravo watch Charlie fish in the Delta, and hear an Echo. Spell your own name out loud with it every day, then try street signs and license plates. Come back on day 1, 3, 7 and 21.
